messages:
maria: starting canary for fp8-enabled kernel on redwood-13b-v2 across h100/l40s. flagging longseq route since customers reported summary drift.

ploy-bot: canary deployed -> model=redwood-13b-v2, variant=fp8-optimized, pools=[h100-rot, l40s-rot]; config: kv_tiling=enabled, hetero_precision=auto

kevin: rough repro? what dataset and seq len?

maria: running our long-summarization suite (arXiv/long-xsum, books) with seq_len=16k, batch=1. quick snippet from the runtime log showing misaligned offsets when tiling toggles:

```
[2026-03-19T14:03:11Z] runtime/gemm.cu: launching fp8_tiled_gemm(tile=128 stride=1024)
[2026-03-19T14:03:11Z] kv_cache.cc: layer=31 expected_kv_pos=8192 got=8184
[2026-03-19T14:03:11Z] decode: token=2045 logprob delta=-0.0023
```

maria: per-token deltas are tiny but they bias the beam and change sentence ordering in long summaries.

sam: note: when hetero_precision toggles per-tile we sometimes use fp16 kernels for some timesteps on L40S. compounding numerical diff is expected.

joana: bakeoff numbers (3 seeds, mean):
- baseline fp32: rouge-L 32.01
- fp8 kernel canary: rouge-L 31.30 (delta -0.71)
- gptq-int8: rouge-L 30.85 (delta -1.16)
- awq-8bit: rouge-L 31.68 (delta -0.33)
observations: fp8 is closest to baseline but sensitive to kernel consistency with kv tiling.

alex: suspect the hetero_precision handshake uses a per-tile threshold on tile_size; on L40S our runtime used threshold=120 incorrectly, letting some steps hit fp16 path. quick mitigation: bump threshold to 200 or force consistent kernel per-request.

kevin: plan:
1) alex bisect threshold + open PR (owner: alex) — due EOD
2) joana run deterministic longseq bakeoff with forced seeds (owner: joana) — 24h
3) maria patch canary to set hetero_precision=false for seq_len>4096 (owner: maria) — immediate
4) sam add CI regression (4k/8k/16k) assert rouge-delta < 0.5 (owner: sam) — by Friday

maria: applied hotfix: hetero_precision disabled on longseq routes. monitoring next 5 runs.

deploy-bot: canary updated: hetero_precision=false on route=longseq, rollout=partial

joana: also adding a per-token logprob-drift metric to console: gauge=route.token_drift.p99, will emit baseline comparison every minute.

sam: test suggestion: run with kv_tiling=off. if drift disappears then it's definitely tiling+kernel interaction.

maria: running a quick kv_tiling=off run now, will paste short results.

alex: if bisect proves threshold bug, add runtime invariant: kernel_choice must be stable across timesteps for same request_id. That should stop transient switches.

kevin: agree. also add alert if kernel_choice variance > 0.1 across timesteps.

maria: filed shard: INF-4621 "kernel_choice stability invariant" and linked bisect PR when ready. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
